title: Status Epilepticus — Adult Treatment Ladder
sources: Critical Vector — EM Pocket Guide: Status Epilepticus
Kapur J et al. ESETT (levetiracetam vs fosphenytoin vs valproate). NEJM 2019
Glauser T et al. AES status epilepticus guideline. Epilepsy Curr 2016

changelog.change: Initial entry — the time-anchored ladder: benzodiazepine → second-line ASM (ESETT: LEV / fosphenytoin / valproate all equivalent) → anaesthetic infusion → super-refractory options. Doses inline.

summary: SE = a seizure lasting > 5 min, or ≥ 2 seizures without recovery of consciousness between. Treat immediately — neuronal injury accrues after ~30 min, and benzodiazepines get less effective the longer you wait (GABA-A receptors internalise). Give a FULL benzodiazepine dose, then a full second-line agent, then intubate for an infusion.

rows: 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg per dose), may repeat once at 5 min
No IV access: midazolam 10 mg IM/IN, or diazepam 20 mg PR. Under-dosing the benzo is the commonest early error

Fosphenytoin 20 PE/kg IV, OR valproate 40 mg/kg IV — ESETT 2019: all three roughly EQUIVALENT (~45–50% seizure cessation). Pick on comorbidity: avoid valproate in hepatic disease / pregnancy; fosphenytoin has infusion hypotension / bradycardia and is pro-arrhythmic
Propofol 1–2 mg/kg bolus → 1–15 mg/kg/hr, OR midazolam 0.2 mg/kg bolus → 0.05–2 mg/kg/hr
Titrate to seizure cessation, then to burst-suppression on continuous EEG. Watch for PRIS with prolonged high-dose propofol
Super-refractory SE (> 24 h, or recurs on weaning the infusion)
Ketamine 1–1.5 mg/kg → 1–5 mg/kg/hr as an adjunct / alternative (NMDA antagonism — useful as GABA responsiveness fails). Consider ketogenic diet, immunotherapy, magnesium/pyridoxine trials

items: Check glucose immediately — give D50 (+ thiamine 100 mg IV if malnourished / alcohol) for hypoglycaemia.
Basic labs incl. sodium, calcium, magnesium; antiseizure-drug levels if on maintenance therapy; toxicology screen.
For a refractory or first unprovoked seizure: CT head, then LP if meningitis / encephalitis is possible; start empiric aciclovir ± antibiotics if febrile.
In an eclamptic / peripartum patient: magnesium sulfate is first-line (see the pregnancy emergency-drugs module), not a benzodiazepine.
Isoniazid overdose seizure that won't respond to benzos: pyridoxine (gram-for-gram with the ingestion, or 5 g empiric).
Continuous EEG once an infusion is running — up to ~20% of comatose SE patients have ongoing NON-convulsive seizures after the visible activity stops.

buildNote: Tier 1 — adult SE was a gap (peds status is covered in peds-midazolam-status). Non-convulsive SE and the Salzburg EEG criteria are a possible expansion.
